summary: Inventoried Packages/ArrCore/Sources/ArrCore/Services' *arr client stack (HTTPClient, ArrAPIClient, Radarr/Sonarr/Lidarr/WhisparrClient, SearchClient, ArrDownloadClients) plus caches (TitleMetadataStore, LibraryIndex, SearchOptionsCache, CoalescingCache, SeriesIdentityResolver) and the Codable models they decode into. 13 in-scope files, 4512 total LOC, all replaced_by_mediakit=true (transport/clients/caches/identity — no views or view-models in scope). Whisparr has no v2/v3 code path (hard-coded /api/v3; only a v2/v3 naming distinction survives in a category-matching comment in ArrDownloadClients.swift). Sonarr has genuine dual-version logic: setSeasonMonitored tries /api/v5/series/{id}/season first, falls back to the two-PUT V3 season-mutation dance on HTTP 404/405. A major, easy-to-miss finding: fetchQueue/fetchCalendar/fetchHistory on all four arr clients carry NO DemoMode.isActive branch at all — demo substitution for those three happens one layer up (QueueAggregator, per grep). Two ArrAPIClient shared operations (fetchHealth, fetchDiskSpace) also have no demo branch and always hit the real network even in demo mode. ServiceConfig.identityFingerprint hashes only apiKey.count, not the key value, while SearchOptionsCache's own key includes the full apiKey string — two different fingerprint schemes coexist for what is nominally the same 'has the config changed' question.

findings: fetchQueue, fetchCalendar and fetchHistory on ALL FOUR arr clients (Radarr/Sonarr/Lidarr/Whisparr) carry no DemoMode.isActive check whatsoever; demo substitution for these three paths lives one layer up in QueueAggregator (confirmed via grep) rather than in the client, unlike every other operation which is demo-gated inline. This is an architectural inconsistency worth flagging to whoever ports the layer to MediaKit — the new client cannot just be a drop-in replacement guided by grepping the client files alone.

deleteQueueItem, fetchHealth and fetchDiskSpace on ArrAPIClient have NO demo-mode guard at all and always perform the real network call even when DemoMode.isActive is true — likely an oversight (every sibling write operation in the same file has a matching sleep+no-op branch) rather than intentional, since deleteQueueItem is destructive.

Sonarr's setSeasonMonitored is the only genuine cross-version fallback in the whole *arr client layer: it optimistically PUTs /api/v5/series/{id}/season and, only on HTTP 404/405, falls back to a two-step V3 season-mutation dance that deliberately writes the opposite value first to force Sonarr's monitored-cascade to fire even on a no-op toggle (documented at length in-line — this is fragile, undertested surface for a rewrite to preserve exactly).

There is no Whisparr v2-vs-v3 code path anywhere: WhisparrClient hard-codes apiBase = "/api/v3". The only trace of a v2/v3 distinction is a comment in ArrDownloadClients.category() noting that Whisparr v2 uses the field name tvCategory and v3 uses movieCategory — matched generically by suffix, not by an explicit version branch.

Two different 'has this config changed' fingerprint schemes coexist: ServiceConfig.identityFingerprint is `"\(baseURL)|\(apiKey.count)"` (length only, not the key value) and is used by LibraryIndex/SeriesIdentityResolver, while SearchOptionsCache.key builds its own `"\(source)|\(baseURL)|\(apiKey)"` with the full API key. A user who edits their API key but keeps the same length would not invalidate LibraryIndex's cached library snapshot, but would invalidate SearchOptionsCache.

The Radarr/Sonarr/Lidarr DELETE library-record path deliberately sends BOTH addImportExclusion and addImportListExclusion query params on every call because Radarr/Whisparr and Sonarr/Lidarr disagree on the parameter name — ASP.NET silently ignores the one it doesn't recognize. This is documented, deliberate duplication, not dead code.

arr error bodies are the real error source: HTTPError.serverMessage(from:) parses three different arr/ASP.NET error shapes (Servarr array of {errorMessage}, {message} object, ASP.NET ProblemDetails {errors:{field:[...]}}) out of the response body, and 401/403 get a special-cased hint because Servarr returns an EMPTY body for those codes specifically — confirming the memory note that arr errors live in the body, not the status.

ArrAPIClient.resolveMetadata documents that three clients (Radarr/Sonarr/Lidarr) used to have a line-for-line duplicate of the cache-then-bounded-fan-out-then-batch-write logic before being consolidated here — a completed dedup, not a remaining one.

TitleMetadataStore deliberately persists to Application Support (never Caches) as ONE JSON file (not one file per entity) with 30-day touch-based retention and 2-second debounced flush; LibraryIndex is purely in-memory (actor, no persistence) with a 10-minute TTL and per-source in-flight-fetch coalescing keyed by config fingerprint; SearchOptionsCache is MainActor (not actor) with a 15-minute TTL split per-facet (profiles/folders/metadataProfiles) so a partial write from one caller can't blank another caller's slot.

No dead/duplicated decoders were found among the in-scope client files themselves — SearchClient's addAlbum performs an extra GET to /search before the POST to /album specifically to look up the release-group id Lidarr's add endpoint needs, which is a genuine two-request add flow unique to Lidarr (every other addX is a single POST).
open_questions: Whether QueueAggregator's DemoMode.isActive branches (lines ~382 and ~450, confirmed present but not read in full) fully substitute for fetchQueue/fetchCalendar/fetchHistory across all four sources, or only for some — worth a closer read of QueueAggregator.swift (out of this task's file scope) before assuming MediaKit's rewrite can move demo-gating into the client layer unchanged.

Whether the download-client implementations (QbittorrentClient/TransmissionClient/RtorrentClient/DelugeClient/SabnzbdClient/NzbgetClient) — explicitly NOT enumerated by the given file list beyond ArrDownloadClients.swift — are meant to be in the MediaKit communication-layer scope too; they were left out of this inventory per the literal scope list given.
